causes.text: On 2023-07-26, Reuters reported that U.S. equipment makers could face an inventory glut as demand from farmers and construction firms cooled, risking oversupply and pressuring manufacturers' margins; higher borrowing costs had also kept ISM manufacturing PMI below 50 for the eighth straight month.

source_info.title: US machinery makers eye bumper earnings for now, but inventory glut looms

effects.text: On 2024-02-15, Deere cut its 2024 profit forecast as high borrowing rates and softer crop prices curbed big-ticket farm equipment purchases; shares fell about 5.4% after the announcement.

source_info.title: Deere cuts 2024 profit view as borrowing costs hurt farm equipment demand

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Dealers and analysts warned in July 2023 that demand was cooling and an inventory glut could emerge as production stayed elevated; high borrowing costs coincided with eight straight months of sub-50 ISM manufacturing PMI.

Through late 2023, elevated interest rates suppressed orders for agricultural machinery; dealers curtailed purchases to avoid oversupply and manufacturers signaled more cautious production, conditioning a weaker 2024 demand backdrop.
On 2024-02-15, Deere cut its 2024 profit outlook citing farmers' reluctance to buy equipment amid high borrowing costs and lower crop prices; the stock fell about 5.4% following the announcement.

rationale: Mid-2023 warnings about a potential inventory glut and sustained high borrowing costs signaled weakening equipment demand. As dealers reduced orders and financing stayed expensive, Deere faced a softer market and lowered its 2024 profit view, triggering a 5.4% share decline.
counterfactual_analysis: If borrowing costs had eased and dealer inventories stayed balanced, demand would likely have remained firmer, reducing the need for Deere to cut its 2024 profit forecast and likely avoiding the 5.4% stock drop.

adversarial_confounders.text: Extreme weather and the Russia-Ukraine conflict disrupted crop yields and commodity markets in 2023-2024.
adversarial_confounders.impact: These shocks could have reduced farmers' profits and equipment purchases independently of inventory dynamics and interest rates.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - High interest rates and lower crop prices
details.commentary: High interest rates and softer crop prices are macroeconomic headwinds that reduce farmers' appetite and ability to buy expensive equipment. This environment weakens demand across the sector and sets the stage for more cautious profit guidance from manufacturers like Deere.

Warnings about cooling demand and potential inventory gluts signalled an emerging imbalance between production and end-market orders. Deere's later profit forecast cut reflects a balancing adjustment as management recalibrates output, pricing and expectations to align with slower demand conditions.
